<\STATESEP>theory ML_Goal_Test
imports
  ML_Goal
  ML_Utils.ML_Utils
begin<\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>experiment begin

\<comment>\<open>
  Basic usage.
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal test: \<open>
  [@{term "(P \<longrightarrow> Q) \<and> P \<longrightarrow> Q"}]
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. (P \<longrightarrow> Q) \<and> P \<longrightarrow> Q<\STATESEP>apply clarsimp<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal:
No subgoals!<\STATESEP>done<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>thm test

\<comment>\<open>
  A goal that we definitely don't want to write out by hand.

  In this case, we're going to show that if x is less than 10,
  we "only" need to consider the cases when x = 0, or x = 1, or...
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal big_goal: \<open>
  let
    val var_x = Free ("x", @{typ nat});
    val var_P = Free ("P", @{typ bool});
    val max = 10;

    \<comment>\<open>
      @{ML "HOLogic.mk_nat"} produces nested Suc's, which are pretty
      ugly, so we use this instead.
    \<close>
    val mk_nat = HOLogic.mk_number @{typ nat};

    \<comment>\<open>
      Turns (i: int) into @{term "x = i \<Longrightarrow> P"}.
    \<close>
    fun mk_case i =
        let
          val prem = HOLogic.mk_eq (var_x, mk_nat i) |> HOLogic.mk_Trueprop;
          val conc = var_P |> HOLogic.mk_Trueprop;
        in Logic.mk_implies (prem, conc) end

    val x_cases =
        ListExtras.range 0 max
        |> map mk_case;

    val assm =
        HOLogic.mk_binrel @{const_name "less"}
          (var_x,
          (mk_nat max))
        |> HOLogic.mk_Trueprop;

    val goal =
        Logic.list_implies (assm :: x_cases, var_P |> HOLogic.mk_Trueprop)

  in [goal] end
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. \<lbrakk>x < 10; x = 0 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 1 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 2 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 3 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 4 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 5 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 6 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 7 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 8 \<Longrightarrow> P; x = 9 \<Longrightarrow> P\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> P<\STATESEP>by force

\<comment>\<open>
  Names are optional.
\<close><\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal \<open>
  [@{term "True"}]
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. True<\STATESEP>by (rule TrueI)

\<comment>\<open>
  Multiple goals are supported, and result in similar
  "list of fact" lemmas
\<close><\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal multiple_goals: \<open>
  [@{term "(P \<Longrightarrow> Q \<Longrightarrow> P)"}, @{term "(P \<Longrightarrow> Q \<Longrightarrow> Q)"}]
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. (\<lbrakk>P; Q\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> P) &&& (\<lbrakk>P; Q\<rbrakk> \<Longrightarrow> Q)<\STATESEP>by simp+<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>thm multiple_goals[OF TrueI]

\<comment>\<open>
  Handles mixes of @{typ bool} and @{typ prop}.
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal \<open>
  [@{term "PROP A \<Longrightarrow> PROP A"}, @{term "B \<longrightarrow> B"}]
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. (PROP A \<Longrightarrow> PROP A) &&& B \<longrightarrow> B<\STATESEP>by simp+

\<comment>\<open>
  Turns out a lemma name can refer to nothing as well!
\<close><\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal nothing: \<open>[]\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal:
No subgoals!<\STATESEP>done<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>thm nothing[OF TrueI]

\<comment>\<open>
  Attributes can be applied, just like normal lemmas.
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>definition magic where "magic = (5 :: nat)"<\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>ML_goal declared_with_an_attribute[folded magic_def, simp]: \<open>
  [@{term "(5 :: nat) = 2 + 3"}]
\<close><\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. 5 = 2 + 3<\STATESEP>by simp<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>lemma uses_our_new_magic_simp_rule:
  "magic = 1 + 4"<\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>proof (prove)
goal (1 subgoal):
 1. magic = 1 + 4<\STATESEP>by simp<\STATESEP>1<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>end<\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP><\STATESEP>end<\STATESEP>0<\TRANSEP>
